about: Anchored HUD clusters for ui_layout.py (w733). Each member is the union of everything drawn under that object; its edges are measured against the anchor's, and a change over the tolerance between before and after fails. Names are object names in main.unity (HudCornerSpacing.cs names the bottom-right ones). OptionToggles is the column of slide-out toggles; its parent QuckControls also holds the slide-outs themselves, which move when opened, so it is not a member. The edges key limits a cluster to the edges that should hold (a panel whose height follows its content keeps only its left and top). Add a cluster when you change one. openedPanels classifies the elements a player opens on purpose and can close (w742): they may cover the HUD, and ui_layout.py checks them instead of counting their overlaps.

openedPanels.why: A panel or slide-out the player opens on purpose and can close may draw over HUD elements (the hotbar, the Objectives card, the minimap buttons). ui_layout.py does not count its overlaps with the HUD; it checks that the panel draws on top, takes the clicks over everything it covers, stays inside the screen, and that closing it leaves the covered HUD where it was. Overlaps between always-on HUD blocks, anchored-cluster drift and colour mismatches still fail.

openedPanels.howToAdd: Add a path (components joined with /, fnmatch globs, matched against a run of components anywhere in the element's path, '(Clone)' ignored) only for something the player opens on purpose and can close again. Never for something always showing, and never to make a check pass: a HUD piece in the way of another HUD piece is a defect.

backdrops.why: A full-screen view the HUD is drawn over is not an HUD block: what lies on it does not overlap it in any sense a player sees (w959: the Map Controls row always lies on the map view, and Map x MapControls failed every check that moved the controls, 110684 -> 43499 px2, exit 1 in all eight census pairs).
who: Ben, w959, 2026-10-10: "just move the buttons to the top next to the player panel" (the controls belong to the map view)
backdrops.howToAdd: Only a view that fills the screen behind the whole HUD, never a panel or an HUD element. Same path syntax as openedPanels.

windowOverlaps.why: No overlaps in the UI (Ben: "UI should be clean and flowy"). ui_layout.py lists every overlap that involves an open window (openedPanels above): window against window, and window against an always-on HUD block, each named with both elements and the overlap rect. An overlap passes only when it is listed under `allowed` with the requester's own words (and the condition they set), or is a window the dock hosts. Every other one is NOT ALLOWED: new or kept between windows the change moved fails ui_layout.py check and pr_evidence.py (w981: the Station strip stood 11 px over the Player Inventory in the Deck's classic layout and `overlaps` said 0).
windowOverlaps.howToAdd: Only for an overlap the requester asked for, with their words word for word in `who` (the last entry is printed next to the overlap), the two sides as path patterns (components joined with /, fnmatch globs, '(Clone)' ignored, matched against a run of components anywhere in an element's path) and, when their words set a condition, `when`. Never to make a check pass, and never wider than the words: a quote about one pair allows that pair, in the situation they described. `when` supports aStandsAbove: the named element (a path tail), meaning the `a` window stands directly over it.

hosting.source: docs/UI-Architecture.md in the game repo (develop), the building dock: "a selected building's EntityPanel windows dock frameless, as tabs" in StructuredDock, so a building panel inside the dock's frame is its tab, not an overlap
